notes: All 92 pages read end to end: the preface, contributors and methodology; the five historic context chapters (early apartment buildings before 1906, the Reconstruction era 1906-1915, post-Reconstruction expansion 1916-1938, early public and war-time housing 1938-1945, and post-war multi-family housing 1945-1978); the architectural characteristics chapter with its building forms and building features; the nine architectural style sections; the five evaluation-criteria frameworks with their worked examples; and the bibliography. It is a citywide thematic statement with no appendix inventory, no APNs and no per-property status codes. Its address-level yield comes from three seams: the figure captions, which almost always give an architect and a build year; the type examples named in the narrative, which add the reason the building is being pointed at (its parking arrangement, its courtyard, its adjacent garage); and the worked examples at the end of each evaluation-criteria section, which carry an explicit eligibility finding. Because the subject is the buildings themselves, nearly every address it prints carries an architect, a build year, or both.
